subject: Hosted IO tiers and model compatibility — pricing inquiry
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@cereshealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-20T08:13:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted IO pricing & model roster for evaluation

Hi Irene,

We are kicking off an evaluation of hosted inference vendors for an upcoming patient-facing summarization feature. Can you share your standard per-1M token IO pricing (separate input / output rates) for the hosted API and a current list of supported models (including quantized or low-cost variants if available)?

Also helpful to know:
- Typical latency expectations for chat workloads at 2–4k context lengths (p50/p95) for the models you recommend,
- Any published discount tiers for committed monthly volume (baseline and escalators),
- Whether SOC2 and a data processing addendum are available to sign.

We'd like a baseline rate card and anything you can share pre-contract so procurement can start internal evaluation. I've CC'd our procurement mailbox.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call if it helps.

Samira Khan
Product Lead, Ceres Health
samira@cereshealth.com

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@cereshealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, procurement@cereshealth.com
Date: 2026-05-20T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted IO pricing & model roster for evaluation

Hi Samira — thanks for the note and context. Happy to help.

Quick answers and next steps:
- I attached our current Hosted IO rate card (Redwood-Hosted-IO-Ratecard-v1.pdf) which shows per-1M token input / output rates across our catalog. Prices vary by model family and whether you pick the standard or quantized variant.
- We also included a short SLA & DPA stub (SLA-and-Data-processing-addendum.pdf) — we are SOC 2 Type II compliant and can provide the report through an NDA process.
- Discount tiers: baseline is a standard published set; we have stacked discounts for committed monthly spends (I list ranges in the attached). If you can share a rough monthly token expectation, I can run a formal example with tiered pricing and an estimated monthly invoice.
- Latency: for chat at 2–4k context, p50/p95 varies by model. Examples in the rate card — generally smaller 7–13B families hit p50 ~80–160ms and p95 ~300–700ms on our hosted fleet; largest families are higher. If you need specific p95 targets we can propose a Dedicated or priority routing configuration.

Can you confirm expected monthly tokens, and whether the primary workload is streaming chat or batch generation? I can loop in Marissa (cc'd) for pricing exceptions and contract-level questions.

If you'd prefer, here's a short link to the hosted model catalog: https://drive.google.com/open?id=hosted-ratecard-2026

Best,
Irene Choi
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Samira Khan <samira@cereshealth.com>

Date: 2026-05-21T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted IO pricing & model roster for evaluation

Thanks, Irene — got the attachments and took a first pass. A few clarifications from procurement / product:

- Expected monthly volume: initial pilot ~6M tokens/month, production target ~45M tokens/month within 6–8 months. Peak day could be ~2.5M tokens.
- Primary workload: streaming chat summaries of visit notes (2–3 turns per session), latency sensitivity moderate (p95 ideally <700ms for user experience).
- Interested in lower-cost quantized variants if accuracy tradeoffs are minimal. Are there per-1M IO rates for quantized options in the rate card or are those custom?
- Procurement asked for a simple example: baseline hosted pricing for 1M, 10M, and 50M token months (input/output split) plus discount thresholds. They also want an estimated monthly cost when applying prefix/KV caching savings assumptions (they estimate ~20% token reduction after warmup).

I've attached a short procurement question workbook (CerES_Procurement_Questions.xlsx) for fields they'd like filled. Can you produce a short formal quote or example invoice so we can move to an internal greenlight?

Samira

Subject: Re: Hosted IO pricing & model roster for evaluation

Samira — thanks for the volumes and workbook. I pulled together a short baseline summary below (high level; I can convert to a one-page formal quote once you confirm model family choice and whether quantized variants are acceptable):

Baseline per-1M token rates (hosted API, USD) — representative examples- small / low-cost family (6–8B, quantized variant available): input $120 / output $240 per 1M tokens- medium family (13B standard): input $250 / output $500 per 1M tokens- large family (70B standard): input $900 / output $1,800 per 1M tokens

Discount schedule (committed monthly spend, applied to invoice):
- Commit >= $50k/mo: 5% off list
- Commit >= $150k/mo: 10% off list
- Enterprise multiyear commitments: custom pricing (typically >15% with additional credits for onboarding)

Quantized variants: Available for select families — typically ~40–55% lower per-1M token costs vs. standard floats; we note modest output-quality delta on certain instruction-following tests. Quantized pricing is listed in the attached rate card under the model entries. For your use case, we recommend testing a quantized 13B variant in a short eval (we can provide a 2-week trial on a dev key).

Caching assumptions: applying a conservative 20% effective token reduction from prefix/KV caching reduces monthly spend proportionally; we can include a modeled example in the formal quote.

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm which model family you'd like us to baseline (6–8B quantized or 13B standard).
2) We produce a one-page formal quote with the 1M/10M/50M examples, caching assumptions, and expected invoice totals.
3) optional pricing call this week to walk procurement through the numbers (30 min).

Links: hosted rate card (public snippet) — https://drive.google.com/open?id=hosted-ratecard-2026
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/672341

If helpful I can deliver the formal quote by end of day tomorrow once you confirm the family.

Best,
